messages:
Sophia: FYI customer 'ClearPay' hit a spike of 429s *right after* their monthly quota reset. They reported a wave of errors for ~3m then a billing spike. Can we triage?
Ben: Which SDK/version and how are they sending requests (parallel workers / retries)?
Sophia: SDK v1.4.2 (official JS). They run 50 worker processes that queue requests when throttled and replay them after the window resets. Attached logs show a tight retry loop after reset. No Retry-After header observed in many 429 responses.
Alex: Hmm. If clients replay queued work immediately when quota flips, that can create a thundering-herd at t=reset. Do we see any `X-RateLimit-Reset` or `Retry-After` values?
Sophia: Sample response header we got: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nContent-Type: application/json\nX-Request-Id: abc123\n` — no Retry-After, no reset header in a bunch of entries. Logs: `worker=17 attempt=1 status=429` repeated.
Maya: Sounds like two problems stacked: (1) server not consistently returning rate-limit metadata; (2) clients are replaying en masse. If client retry policy has little/no jitter, you'll see immediate replays. Do we know the SDK default retry/backoff?
Ben: Current JS SDK v1.4.2 defaults: up to 3 retries, fixed 100ms base backoff + linear increments, *no* jitter. That combination + queued backlog is very volatile.
Alex: That matches pattern. Without jitter/expo backoff, many clients align and slam right after reset. Also if requests are non-idempotent, retries can cause duplicate side effects/billing.
Sophia: The customer says a few duplicate charges happened for idempotent-intended endpoints. They weren't setting `Idempotency-Key`.
Maya: Immediate mitigation for them: 1) instruct to set `Idempotency-Key` for write operations, 2) reduce worker concurrency, 3) upgrade SDK or patch retry config to a randomized backoff. We should also ensure our endpoints include `Retry-After` or `X-RateLimit-Reset` consistently.
Ben: Quick suggested client config (JS SDK):
```
client.configureRetries({
  maxRetries: 5,
  backoff: 'exponential',
  baseMs: 200,
  maxMs: 5000,
  jitter: 'full'
});
// also: ensure request header 'Idempotency-Key' = uuid
```
Alex: On the server side we can: A) add `Retry-After` for 429s during quota windows, B) add a small rolling-release window at gateway for customers with heavy backlogs (leaky bucket), C) check billing dedupe using idempotency metadata.
Sophia: Can infra add temporary leaky-bucket smoothing for ClearPay while we engage them? They are an enterprise customer.
Maya: I'll ping infra/ingress. Short-term we can also add a note to support playbook telling customers to avoid replaying queued requests at exact reset and to randomize reconnection.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026 - "ClearPay post-quota replay causing 429s & duplicate ops"
Ben: I'll draft a small patch to SDK default retry policy (expo + jitter + honor `Retry-After`) and a doc snippet for support. If infra adds gateway smoothing and we ensure 429 headers, this should prevent repetition.
Sophia: Action items: 1) Maya -> ask infra for leaky-bucket for ClearPay (P1), 2) Ben -> prepare SDK patch + docs (target: minor release), 3) Support -> advise ClearPay to set Idempotency-Key + throttle workers, 4) Alex -> validate billing dedupe for affected timeframe. Escalate to eng-runtime if we see continued customer impact.
Ben: Also note: advise customers to avoid 'bulk replay after reset' pattern; suggest exponential backoff with full jitter and request-level idempotency.
Sophia: I'll notify the customer with these mitigations and keep thread updated. Thanks!
